data.title: Key deals this week: Option Care Health, PTC, Energy Transfer and more
data.description:
Here's a list of key deals reported across sectors this week:

  • Service Properties Trust (SVC) was surging after the hospitality investment firm TKO LLC proposed to acquire the former's entire hospitality portfolio for $2.0B.
  • Viatris (VTRS) and Pacira BioSciences (PCRX) said they entered into a definitive agreement under which Viatris will acquire all outstanding shares of Pacira for $36.50 per share in cash, representing an aggregate equity value of $1.65B.
  • Option Care Health (OPCH) shares jumped 34% in early trading on Tuesday after CD&R and McKesson (MCK) announced a definitive agreement to acquire the company for $32.05 per share, valuing it at approximately $5.8 billion including debt.
  • Energy Transfer (ET) said Tuesday it agreed to acquire Vaquero Midstream in a $2.625B deal consisting of $1.95B in cash and ~33.3M newly issued Energy Transfer common units.
  • Canadian utility ​companies Emera (EMA) and Canadian Utilities (CDUAF) said Tuesday they agreed to a ​merger in an all-stock transaction worth C$14.3B (US$10B), creating ​a combined company with a C$72B enterprise value and a regulated rate base of C$45B serving ~6M customers across Canada, the U.S., and international markets.
  • Cenovus Energy (CVE) said Monday it agreed to acquire Athabasca Oil (ATHOF) in a cash-and-stock deal valued at ~C$5.7B, representing a 14% premium to Athabasca's 20-day volume-weighted average trading price.
  • Schneider Electric SE (SBGSF) said it has agreed to acquire U.S.-based engineering software developer PTC Inc. (PTC) for $22.6 billion (€20.1 billion). The French conglomerate will buy PTC for $205 per share in an all-cash deal, it said in a statement.
  • CCC Intelligent Solutions (CCC) soared 13% in after-hours trading on a report that private equity firm GTCR and Elliott Investment Management are in advanced discussions to purchase the car-insurance software firm.

data.title: Nvidia in talks to buy ‘open’ model startup Reflection AI: FT
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) is holding discussions to acquire or increase its investment in Reflection AI, a U.S. startup focused on developing open-weight models, the Financial Times reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the discussions.

Talks between the companies are at an early stage, and the structure of a potential deal could take several forms, including a so-called 'acqui-hire,' which allows tech giants to hire staff and license technology, avoiding antitrust scrutiny linked to a full acquisition.

Deal terms currently under discussion were not available. Nvidia (NVDA), the world’s most valuable company, has already invested $800M into Reflection, which was last valued at $25B in a March funding round.

Nvidia (NVDA), whose CEO Jensen Huang has in the past called for an open-weight “ecosystem” for AI, could also make an additional equity investment in Reflection or reach an agreement to supply more chips or computing power to the company.

A deal could be reached in the coming weeks, said multiple people with knowledge of the matter, cautioning that companies also could walk away from the talks. Nvidia (NVDA) and Reflection didn’t respond to FT’s requests for comment.

data.title: Cliffs unit is said to proceed with Canada layoffs despite govt. ultimatum
data.description:
Cleveland-Cliffs’ (CLF) unit Stelco has informed the Canadian government that it is proceeding with hundreds of job cuts at its production sites in Ontario despite an ultimatum issued by Ottawa earlier this week to avoid the layoffs, the Globe and Mail reported on Saturday.

On Sept. 28, Stelco announced plans to lay off up to 500 steelworkers in Hamilton and Nanticoke, Ont., noting that it couldn’t operate profitably mainly due to the impact of elevated U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel.

When the federal government approved Cliffs’ (CLF) $3.4B acquisition of Stelco in 2024, the Cleveland-based steelmaker agreed to several legally binding terms, including a condition to maintain at least the same number of unionized workers in Canada for five years.

On Monday, Canadian Industry Minister Mélanie Joly issued a five-day ultimatum forcing the company to come up with a plan to comply with its employment guarantees under the Investment Canada Act or face possible legal action.

Citing a legal provision related to the pledges and the government’s ICA guidelines, Stelco’s president and general counsel Paul Simon said in a letter to Joly that the company has not breached its commitments.

A spokesperson for Joly confirmed receiving the letter.

“Your representation that Stelco’s planned layoffs cause it to breach its undertakings is false,” Simon said in the letter, implying that tariffs could allow non-enforcement or renegotiation of the commitments.

“Throughout the history of the Investment Canada Act and its predecessor foreign investment acts, it has consistently been understood that changes in circumstances may necessitate the non-enforcement or renegotiation of undertakings,” Simon added.

data.title: China passenger vehicle retail market slumps 24% in September
data.description:
An YTD slump in the passenger vehicle market in China extended last month, with retail sales for September totaling roughly 1.7M, a 24% decline from a year ago, according to preliminary data released by the China Passenger Car Association on Saturday.

While YTD retail sales fell 21% YoY to ~13.4M, the broader passenger vehicle market expanded from August, with passenger vehicle retail sales climbing ~10% from a month ago, driven by new energy vehicles.

Retail sales of passenger NEVs stood at ~1.1M in September, down ~12% YoY but accounting for ~67% of total passenger vehicle retail sales for the month.

YTD retail NEV sales totaled ~7.8M, down 12% YoY and signaling a weak domestic market, while wholesale passenger NEV sales reached ~11.4M YTD, up 10% from a year ago, as CPCA said higher oil prices remained elevated longer than expected, fueling exports.

The local markets also faced tough comps from a year earlier when sales climbed thanks to a rush to buy new vehicles before some Chinese regions reined in trade-in subsidies.

BYD (BYDDF) (BYDDY), Geely Auto (GELYF), Chery (CRYAF) (CRAUY), Leapmotor (ZJLMF), and Tesla (TSLA) were among the top 10 manufacturers in the passenger NEV wholesale market last month.

Companies including XPeng (XPEV) (XPNGF), Li Auto (LI), and Nio (NIO) were ranked outside the top ten.

data.title: Flight disruptions growing after missile attack on Saudi airport
data.description:
Saudi Arabia is grappling with a surge in flight disruptions after a blast at the international airport in the kingdom’s capital, Riyadh, wounded many people and led to evacuations on Saturday, according to two regional officials.

A missile struck a passenger terminal and many people were wounded, one of the officials said. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak to the media. Ambulances were seen rushing toward the airport.

Flights to Riyadh diverted elsewhere, the Flightradar24 tracker said, almost four hours after the last flight landed at 2:05 p.m. Kuwait Airways said it was canceling flights because the airport had closed. Canada’s embassy advised citizens to avoid all travel to the airport, noting “ongoing military activity.”

King Khalid International Airport has been targeted multiple times in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen. The Houthis claimed responsibility for the earlier attacks, including one Wednesday that killed a Sudanese national.

A resident said he heard explosions in Riyadh

There was no immediate Houthi statement Saturday. The Saudi government-run Center for International Communication, which oversees foreign media in the kingdom, didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

A Riyadh resident, Ahmed Sayed, told The Associated Press he heard at least two loud explosions that rocked the capital.

The airport issued a terse alert telling passengers to check their flight status with airlines before heading to the airport. At least 225 flights at the airport had been canceled over the past 24 hours, according to flight-tracking site FlightAware.

Fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces has escalated, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support for government forces in an attempt to reverse recent Houthi gains along the Red Sea.

The rebels' gains gave them better surveillance of shipping on a corridor that's a crucial alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships.

Though the Houthis have told the AP and others they are only targeting Saudi shipping as part of a blockade in retaliation for one imposed on them, concerns about wider attacks persist. The Houthis previously attacked other ships after the war in Gaza began, calling it solidarity with Palestinians. A U.S. bombing campaign ended that.

Trump ‘not happy’ but no sign of new support

The Saudis have sought support from the U.S. and other allies as its airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure have come under attack. Officials said U.S. assistance has included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the latest offensive.

On Friday, as he left the White House, U.S. President Donald Trump was asked about the attacks on the Riyadh airport and told reporters, “It’s not good” and “I’m not happy.” But there has been no immediate sign of U.S. military support to respond to the attacks.

The Saudi and Omani foreign ministers spoke by phone about the importance of “supporting diplomatic solutions to de-escalate tensions” in the region, the kingdom said Saturday. Oman, which lies across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, has played a mediator role at times in the region.

Meanwhile, Saudi authorities warned the public this week that "filming, publishing or sharing information related to countering missiles and drones and their impact sites exposes you to legal liability.”

Flight disruptions are growing

This week, the Houthis warned global airlines “for the last time” about the potential consequences of operating in Saudi airspace, which they described as a theater for their military operations.

Air India, FlyDubai, Lufthansa Group and Pakistan International Airlines have been among the airlines suspending flights to and from Riyadh and other Saudi airports for the next few days.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency has expanded its guidance on Saudi airspace, noting the Houthis’ ability to strike targets deeper inside the kingdom, including Riyadh, and a “greater focus on aviation infrastructure.”

The missile and drone attacks and interception efforts “create an increased risk of misidentification of civil aircraft,” it said.

In Thursday’s attack, the Saudi national carrier said one of its aircraft was damaged while it was on the ground, with no passengers on board.

Dear readers, we recognize that politics often intersects with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion. 

The Associated Press contributed to this story.

data.title: Philips investors’ move to probe company over 2021 recall denied by Dutch court
data.description:
A court in Amsterdam on Saturday denied demands by shareholders of Philips (PHG) for an investigation into the company over its handling of a massive product recall involving its sleep apnea and ventilator machines in 2021.

The Enterprise Chamber of the Amsterdam Court of Appeal ruled in favor of the company, dealing a setback to a large group of Philips (RYLPF) shareholders, including the Dutch investors’ association, VEB, and several institutional investors.

The shareholders called for a court inquiry after the Dutch medtech launched a recall of roughly 3.5M breathing machines in 2021 due to concerns that a polyurethane foam used in the devices could deteriorate and become toxic.

The investors argued that the company failed to identify and address the issues promptly due to weaknesses in its internal systems, the chambers said. They also alleged that the Philips (PHG) board of directors was aware of the problems at the company’s Respironics U.S. unit, which made the devices, well before the disclosures were made regarding the issue.

“There is also no reason to assume that Philips ought to have intervened at Respironics earlier, or that the Supervisory Board exercised insufficient oversight,” Bloomberg reported, quoting the chamber. It added that there is no sufficient basis to determine that Philips' (PHG) disclosures to the investors were “late, incorrect, or misleading.”

The chamber didn’t rule on whether there were errors at Respironics or regarding the extent of liability for damages faced by investors.

data.title: Real estate stocks outperform broader markets
data.description:
Real estate stocks edged up in a week that saw the broader AI sector face a reality check, and the Federal Open Market Committee's September meeting minutes reveal united support for the central bank's tightening cycle.

The tech-heavy indexes came under pressure amid a wider impact on AI trade due to revenue concerns surrounding OpenAI. Reports indicated that OpenAI's annualized revenue reached $50B at the end of September, below the $68B figure reported the previous month.

Semiconductor stocks dragged down the Nasdaq Composite Index for the week.

Meanwhile, most Fed officials expected that another rate increase would be appropriate by the end of the year even as they raised their benchmark rate in September, according to minutes from the FOMC's Sept. 15-16 meeting released on Wednesday.

"In my opinion, the week had one real twist: the rapid shift in investor sentiment following the release of OpenAI's revenue data. That was all it took for investors to sell off AI-related stocks following confusion over different revenue reporting methods," said Seeking Alpha analyst Agar Capital.

Utilities and energy gained the most for the week, largely due to a defensive rotation within sectors, according to Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman.

The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 1.79% week-over-week to 266.03 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) was up 1.96% to $41.61.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index advanced 1.26%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 1.23%.

Weekly Winners & Losers

Telecom tower REIT stocks led the largecap gainers after investment firm Grain Management said SpaceX (SPCX) is set to acquire 100% of its nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio.

Crown Castle (CCI) was up 19.87% from the previous week to $79.64. SBA Communications (SBAC) was 15.14% up to $182.49, while American Tower (AMT) was up 12.36% to $182.24.

Healthpeak Properties (DOC) and Omega Healthcare Investors (OHI) topped the losers as healthcare subsidies expired, retreating 3.54% and 2.87% to $18.80 and $44.41, respectively.

The REITs were falling amid increased Medicare costs as the nation ages.

Among midcap stocks, Fermi (FRMI) led the losers, dropping 14.89% week-over-week to $3.43.

The company completed a draft environmental impact statement for its plan to construct and operate four AP1000 reactors at its Project Matador Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus in Texas. A 45-day public comment period on the draft EIS opened on October 9, which runs through November 23.

Millrose Properties (MRP) and Opendoor Technologies (OPEN) followed, with a 9.14% and 9.02% pull back to $22.36 and $2.22, respectively.

Rayonier (RYN) was the winner in the category, adding 5.09% to $18.98.

Among smallcap movers, Empire State Realty (ESBA) (+18.18% W/W to $4.55), Service Properties Trust (SVC) (+12.07% W/W to $7.15), Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) (+11.03% W/W to $4.63), Arbor Realty Trust (ABR) (-19.38% W/W to $2.87), Uniti Group (UNIT) (-14.55% W/W to $6.87), and CBL & Associates Properties (CBL) (-11.32% W/W to $48.51) stood out.

The week saw Service Properties Trust declare a $0.05/share quarterly dividend, in line with previous. However, the stock surged after the hospitality investment firm TKO LLC proposed to acquire the former's entire hospitality portfolio for $2.0B.

Empire State Realty Trust was trading higher after an SEC filing showed that activist investment firm Erez Asset Management now owns over a 5% stake in the office REIT. Bruce Schanzer's Erez Asset Management owns a 5.8% stake in the company.

data.title: Hospital group files lawsuit to stop 340B rebate pilot again
data.description:
The American Hospital Association has once again filed a lawsuit to halt a new pilot that tests a revised rebate model for the 340B Drug Pricing Program, a federal benefits program for underinsured and low-income Americans.

The AHA, the Maine Hospital Association, and four safety-net hospitals filed the suit on Thursday, naming the Health and Human Services Department and the Health Resources and Services Administration, the HHS unit overseeing the program, among its defendants.

The lawsuit was filed in a federal court in Maine days after the HRSA announced the pilot, which allows 10 pharmaceutical manufacturers to offer after-the-fact rebates instead of upfront discounts on 21 drugs purchased under the program.

The Trump administration’s first 340B rebate pilot, which applied to only 10 medicines, was blocked by a federal judge in December following a lawsuit from the AHA and several hospital systems. The HHS formally withdrew the plan in January after losing on appeal.

The latest complaint seeks a temporary and permanent block on the program, which is set to take effect on Jan. 1 with the participation of drugmakers including AbbVie (ABBV), Amgen (AMGN), Astellas (ALPMF), AstraZeneca (AZN), Bristol Myers (BMY), GSK (GSK), Merck (MRK), Pfizer (PFE), and Teva (TEVA).

It makes arguments similar to the first, noting that the pilot doesn’t account for substantial costs the providers will have to incur by purchasing the drugs at market prices and then applying for rebates.

Listed hospital systems: HCA Healthcare (HCA), Community Health Systems (CYH), Surgery Partners (SGRY), Tenet Healthcare (THC), Universal Health Services (UHS), Select Medical Holdings (SEM), Acadia Healthcare (ACHC), LifeStance Health Group (LFST)

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Procter & Gamble, Palantir and SentinelOne among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the green on Friday, with Nasdaq (COMP:IND) and Dow (DJI) advancing 0.64% and 0.8%. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Evercore ISI upgrades Procter & Gamble

Procter & Gamble (PG) was upgraded to Outperform from In line by Evercore, which raised its PT to $166 from $161, citing improving U.S. execution, stabilizing category volumes, and signs that the company’s new organization is beginning to deliver.

Analyst Robert Ottenstein raised its fiscal first-quarter organic sales growth estimate to about 3%, versus a consensus of 2%, saying the quarter could mark the “end of downside risk” to P&G’s sales. They also expect the company to exit fiscal 2027 growing about 4%, a pace it said should support operating leverage.

Palatir upgraded on recent underperformance

Palantir (PLTR) was upgraded by Goldman Sachs from Neutral to Buy, citing recent underperformance.

“The two key debates we hear from investors at Palantir's current $8B revenue run rate and ~100% growth rate are 1) has the best part of Palantir's AI opportunity already been realized, or is the market deep enough for another set of higher revisions? And 2) how sustainable is the FDE model? Our primary takeaway from our most recent set of industry conversations is that the stock is setting up for another phase of outperformance into 2027,” said analyst Gabriela Borges.

The brokerage put a PT of $230 on the stock.

GlobalFoundries downgraded by BNP Paribas

GlobalFoundries (GFS) was downgraded by BNP Paribas to Neutral from Outperform as the investment firm said it sees the growth drivers for the semiconductor foundry as “priced in.”

“We remain optimistic on GlobalFoundries' growth plan and capability to diversify into higher margin optical, satcom, and automotive power applications,” BNP analyst Karl Ackerman wrote. “However, we believe these will be more gradual than current projections. Coupled with structural headwinds limiting Smart Mobile growth, we take a more conservative approach to the company's growth outlook.”

Ackerman also cut his price target to $51 from $80, adding that geopolitical concerns may be a concern for the company.

SentinelOne downgraded on CrowdStrike concerns

SentinelOne (S) was downgraded to Sector Perform from Outperform at FBN Securities, as the investment firm cited concerns about CrowdStrike (CRWD) encroaching on its business.

“The business has improved – NG operating margin% reached a record 10.5% in FQ2 2027, RPO accelerated to 45% Y/Y and AI security ARR roughly tripled – but at $25.43 the shares have moved through our target and more than doubled from the April low, while CrowdStrike keeps taking a larger share of incremental ARR than S’s share of the installed base,” FBN analyst Shebly Seyrafi wrote in a note to clients. “Net, we see a balanced risk/reward from here.”

BNP Paribas raised its Nvidia (NVDA) price target to $345 from $285, citing the company's broad range of AI hardware, CUDA software, and networking products. The brokerage also raised Intel's (INTC) price target to $125 from $75 while maintaining a Neutral rating, saying it could benefit from rising demand for server CPUs as AI agents require more computing power.

Citi upped its price target on AMD (AMD) to $800 from $575 as the investment firm said it now sees the CPU market hitting $300B by 2030.
